brief: A machined aluminium shaft collar. The outer diameter is 25 mm and it is 15 mm long. A 12 mm bore runs all the way through on the axis. Two 4 mm set screw holes pass through the wall from the outside into the bore, 90 degrees apart, both halfway along the length. It carries no load - it is a locating collar, so there is no load case.

implied: The set screw holes are located on the outer surface of the collar.
stated: There are two 4 mm set screw holes.
The set screw holes are 90 degrees apart.
The set screw holes are halfway along the length.
intent.summary: A machined aluminium shaft collar with an outer diameter of 25 mm, a length of 15 mm, and a 12 mm bore running through the axis. Two 4 mm set screw holes are located 90 degrees apart, halfway along the length.
unstated: The collar does not carry any load.

note: requirements: the record as the run accepted it. The answer is the designer's, returned identically twice: one cylinder carrying the `set_screw` tag, nothing declared, no bore and no set screw holes.

notes: dropped REQ_SF_BEARING: the brief states this part carries no load, so there is no load case to take a margin against and nothing could have computed one
dropped 1 load question(s): the brief states that this part carries no load, so there was nothing to be uncertain about
`feature_count:set_screw_hole:mounting` names no feature kind, so it was read as `feature_count:hole:set_screw`.

added REQ_BOUNDING_BOX_X and REQ_BOUNDING_BOX_Y at 25 mm: the brief calls the part square or round at its largest stated size, and nothing in the requirement set measured the part's size at all. A dimension parameter is declared just as truthfully by a plate 30 by 12 as by a plate 30 by 30, and one was: sixteen claims, every one green, and the plate was 30 by 12.

added REQ_ANGLE at 90 deg, measured between the two `set_screw` `hole` features on the built part: the brief states the angle and nothing in the requirement set carried it. Bound to the geometry rather than to a declared parameter, because a design can declare `angle = 90 deg` and drill both holes parallel -- one did, and every other gate passed, because they were real holes that cut real material and nothing looked at where they pointed.

added REQ_ROUND: the brief calls this part round, and two equal bounding boxes do not say a part is round -- a 25 mm square block has a 25 by 25 box exactly as a 25 mm cylinder does. One run asked for a shaft collar and got a square block with both extent claims passing. This measures the built surface: 1 is a cylinder, a square is 0.707.

added REQ_HOLES_12MM_ON_AXIS: the brief states 1 open hole of 12 mm down the part's axis, counted on the built part by diameter. A claim bound to a hole's parameter passes whenever some hole reads that parameter -- a collar had both set screws drawn at the bore's 12 mm, and no bore, and it passed.

added REQ_HOLES_4MM: the brief states 2 open holes of 4 mm, counted on the built part by diameter. A claim bound to a hole's parameter passes whenever some hole reads that parameter -- a collar had both set screws drawn at the bore's 12 mm, and no bore, and it passed.
